plan: Key changes: (1) a React and TypeScript app built by Vite. Before, the repository held only a readme; after, npm run build writes dist and the built page shows the Ada trial heading drawn by React. (2) A Vitest harness. Before, no unit tests; after, npm test runs them with coverage and writes coverage/lcov.info. (3) A Playwright harness. Before, no browser tests; after, npm run test:e2e builds, serves and tests the app in Chromium. (4) A CI workflow that runs all three and reports patch coverage as a commit status. Order: run the existing e2e and unit tests, then TC-1 to TC-5, then the added checks TC-6 to TC-12 from Code review's findings and the new commands, then the walkthrough drive.

decisions: No defect: every designed test passed and AC-1 is met.

Finding, medium, unconfirmed (read in code, medium confidence): the CI coverage step runs scripts/patch-coverage.mjs from the pull request's own checkout with a token that can write commit statuses, so a person with push access could post any status, for example a passing required check. Who notices: nobody, until a false status appears. Path users take: every same-repository pull request. GitHub Actions cannot run here, so I could not prove it.

Finding, low, confirmed (TC-6, high confidence): the unit run passes but, with verbose output, prints 'An update to Root inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)' from the main entry test, whose React root is never unmounted. Developers see the warning; no test fails today.

Finding, low, confirmed (TC-7, high confidence): after the CI Build step, the browser tests build the app again, so every CI run builds and type-checks twice. Developers wait longer; results are correct.

Finding, low, confirmed (TC-8, high confidence): package.json does not list @testing-library/dom; installed with npm's legacy peer setting, the unit run fails with 'Cannot find package @testing-library/dom'. A developer with that common npm setting notices; the default npm ci works (TC-3).

Finding, low, unconfirmed (read in code): on a pull request from a fork the token is read-only, so the coverage status step fails and the job goes red even when coverage is fine. Only fork contributors notice.
Finding, low, unconfirmed (read in code): the coverage status is computed from lcov written by the pull request's own code, so it is advice and should not be a required check.
Finding, low, unconfirmed (read in code): CI actions are pinned to the movable v4 tag beside a status-writing token; first-party actions, low risk.
Explained away: TC-4's first run failed twice on my own path pattern, not on the app; the project's browser run in it passed. Fixed the pattern; the next run passed.
uncertain: TC-2 needs a person: it gathers src/App.tsx, src/main.tsx and the dependency list as attachments and checks the machine-checkable facts, but whether the sources are React components written in TypeScript is the QA person's judgement.
Whether the medium security finding on .github/workflows/ci.yml line 64 should be fixed in this Deliverable.

out/regression.json and the earlier out/report.json in the work folder came from an earlier attempt and said no test earns a lasting place; this run keeps TC-1, TC-3 and TC-4 as coverage tests in test/coverage. I left out/regression.json as I found it; it no longer reflects this run.

suggested_follow_ups: Run the coverage status step from the base branch's copy of scripts/patch-coverage.mjs, or keep the token out of the step that runs pull request code.
Skip the coverage status write on fork pull requests.
Unmount the React root in the main entry test, or render through Testing Library.
Let the Playwright web server reuse a built dist in CI instead of building again.
Pin CI actions to commit hashes.
